title: The Cognitive Revolution (When Machines Do the Thinking)
limitations: Broad historical and macroeconomic essay comparing the transition from physical automation (the Industrial Revolution) to cognitive automation (the Cognitive Revolution). Formulates the Jevons paradox of cognition ('Most problems on Earth currently go un-thought-about, because thinking is expensive'). It provides a conceptual framing of expanding cognitive demand rather than an empirical or operational implementation blueprint.
